questions.questionText: Your enterprise is setting up a new Google Cloud environment. You need complete control over your IP address ranges and want to ensure that no subnets are automatically created, preventing overlap with your on-premises network. Which VPC creation mode is best practice for this requirement?
options: Custom mode VPC
Auto mode VPC
Default VPC
Shared VPC
correctAnswers: Custom mode VPC

explanation.general explanation: A Custom mode VPC network provides you with complete control over your subnets and IP ranges. It does not automatically create subnets, which prevents accidental IP address overlapping with on-premises networks during hybrid cloud setups.

why other options are wrong.Auto mode VPC: Auto mode VPC automatically creates a subnet in each Google Cloud region using a predefined set of IP ranges, which can easily conflict with on-premises networks.
why other options are wrong.Default VPC: The default VPC is an auto mode VPC created automatically in every new project. It is not recommended for enterprise production environments.
why other options are wrong.Shared VPC: Shared VPC allows sharing networks across projects, but the underlying network itself must still be created as either Auto or Custom mode (Custom being the best practice).

questions.questionText: You are designing a globally distributed web application that serves HTTP and HTTPS traffic. You want users around the world to access the application using a single Anycast IP address, and you want traffic routed to the region closest to the user. Which Google Cloud load balancer should you use?
options: Global External Application Load Balancer
External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
External proxy Network Load Balancer
correctAnswers: Global External Application Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: The Global External Application Load Balancer (formerly HTTP/S Load Balancer) is a Layer 7 load balancer that uses a single global Anycast IP address to route HTTP/HTTPS traffic to the closest healthy backend region, providing low latency and global scale.

why other options are wrong.External passthrough Network Load Balanc: This is a regional, Layer 4 load balancer. It does not provide a single global Anycast IP for cross-region routing.
why other options are wrong.Internal Application Load Balancer: This load balancer is strictly for internal traffic within a VPC and cannot be accessed from the public internet.
why other options are wrong.External proxy Network Load Balancer: While global, this load balancer is intended for non-HTTP TCP/SSL traffic, not specifically for HTTP/HTTPS web applications.

questions.questionText: A central networking team needs to manage subnets, IP ranges, and firewall rules for an entire organization, while allowing individual application teams to create and manage their own VM instances in separate projects using those centralized subnets. Which VPC design pattern should you implement?
options: Shared VPC
VPC Network Peering
Multiple standalone VPCs
Cloud VPN between projects
correctAnswers: Shared VPC

explanation.general explanation: Shared VPC allows an organization to connect resources from multiple projects to a common Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network. This architecture separates network administration (in the Host project) from resource provisioning (in the Service projects).

why other options are wrong.VPC Network Peering: VPC Peering connects two completely distinct VPCs. It does not provide centralized management of subnets across projects.
why other options are wrong.Multiple standalone VPCs: This fragments the network administration and forces each application team to manage their own networking.
why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN between projects: Cloud VPN is used for connecting external on-premises networks to GCP, not for sharing subnets between internal GCP projects.

questions.questionText: When configuring a Shared VPC architecture, which two IAM roles are strictly required to allow the networking team to manage the central network and allow developers to attach instances to it?
options: Grant the 'Compute Shared VPC Admin' role to the networking team on the Host project.
Grant the 'Compute Network User' role to the developers on the specific subnets in the Host project.
Grant the 'Compute Network Admin' role to the developers in the Service project.
Grant the 'Project Owner' role to the networking team on all Service projects.
Grant the 'VPC Peering Admin' role to the networking team on the Host project.
correctAnswers: Grant the 'Compute Shared VPC Admin' role to the networking team on the Host project.
Grant the 'Compute Network User' role to the developers on the specific subnets in the Host project.

explanation.general explanation: In a Shared VPC model, the 'Compute Shared VPC Admin' role is required to set up the Host project and attach Service projects. The 'Compute Network User' role allows developers in the Service projects to consume the shared subnets and attach resources like VMs to them.

why other options are wrong.Grant the 'Compute Network Admin' role t: Developers only need to *use* the network, not administer it. Network administration remains in the Host project.
why other options are wrong.Grant the 'Project Owner' role to the ne: This violates the principle of least privilege. The network team does not need to own the application Service projects.
why other options are wrong.Grant the 'VPC Peering Admin' role to th: Shared VPC is a distinct feature from VPC Network Peering; the Peering Admin role does not grant Shared VPC privileges.

questions.questionText: Your application exposes a high-throughput, low-latency UDP service to clients on the internet. All backend virtual machines are located in a single region (us-central1). You need to balance the incoming UDP traffic across these instances. Which load balancer should you use?
options: External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Global External Application Load Balancer
External proxy Network Load Balancer
Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
correctAnswers: External passthrough Network Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: The External passthrough Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and is designed to handle external TCP and UDP traffic within a single region. Because it is passthrough, it is extremely fast and perfect for high-throughput UDP services.

why other options are wrong.Global External Application Load Balance: This is a Layer 7 proxy that only supports HTTP and HTTPS. It does not support UDP traffic.
why other options are wrong.External proxy Network Load Balancer: This proxy load balancer supports TCP traffic but does not support UDP.
why other options are wrong.Internal passthrough Network Load Balanc: While it supports UDP, it is strictly for internal VPC traffic and cannot receive traffic from the public internet.

questions.questionText: Your company acquired another business that also uses Google Cloud. They have their own Google Cloud organization and VPC network. You need to connect their VPC to your VPC so internal applications can communicate using private IP addresses. What is the most straightforward, native Google Cloud networking feature to connect these two distinct VPCs?
options: VPC Network Peering
Shared VPC
Cloud VPN
Cloud Interconnect
correctAnswers: VPC Network Peering

explanation.general explanation: VPC Network Peering allows you to connect two distinct VPC networks natively within Google Cloud, regardless of whether they belong to the same project or different organizations. This enables private IP communication between the networks without routing traffic over the public internet.

why other options are wrong.Shared VPC: Shared VPC is for centrally managing subnets across projects within the *same* organization. It does not bridge two existing, separate VPC networks.
why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN: While you could use a VPN to connect them, it adds unnecessary overhead and limits bandwidth compared to native VPC Network Peering.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Interconnect: Cloud Interconnect is used for connecting on-premises data centers to Google Cloud, not for connecting two cloud VPCs.

questions.questionText: You have an internal microservice running on Compute Engine VMs that receives traffic from a front-end web service located in the same VPC. You need to distribute this HTTP traffic across the internal VMs and perform URL path-based routing, ensuring that all traffic strictly remains on the internal network. Which load balancer is appropriate?
options: Internal Application Load Balancer
Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
External Application Load Balancer
External proxy Network Load Balancer
correctAnswers: Internal Application Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: The Internal Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and is designed for internal HTTP/HTTPS traffic. It supports advanced Layer 7 features like URL path-based routing while keeping all traffic private within the VPC network.

why other options are wrong.Internal passthrough Network Load Balanc: This is a Layer 4 load balancer. It cannot inspect HTTP traffic and therefore cannot perform URL path-based routing.
why other options are wrong.External Application Load Balancer: This is used to distribute traffic coming from the public internet, violating the requirement to keep traffic purely internal.
why other options are wrong.External proxy Network Load Balancer: This is for external TCP/SSL traffic, not internal HTTP traffic with URL routing.

questions.questionText: When configuring a Global External Application Load Balancer to achieve a global Anycast IP address and route traffic to the closest healthy backend, which two specific requirements must be met?
options: The load balancer must use the Premium Network Service Tier.
The load balancer must be configured with a Global Forwarding Rule.
The VPC network must be configured in Auto mode.
The backend services must have Cloud NAT enabled.
The load balancer must use the Standard Network Service Tier.
correctAnswers: The load balancer must use the Premium Network Service Tier.
The load balancer must be configured with a Global Forwarding Rule.

explanation.general explanation: To operate globally and provide a single Anycast IP address, an External Application Load Balancer requires the use of the Premium Network Service Tier (which routes traffic over Google's global backbone) and a Global Forwarding Rule to expose the Anycast IP.

why other options are wrong.The VPC network must be configured in Au: VPC mode (Auto vs Custom) has no bearing on load balancer global routing. Custom mode is actually best practice.
why other options are wrong.The backend services must have Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT is for outbound internet access from private VMs; it has nothing to do with inbound global load balancing.
why other options are wrong.The load balancer must use the Standard: The Standard Network Service Tier restricts networking to a single region and uses public ISPs, breaking global Anycast capabilities.

questions.questionText: You have a VPC subnet configured with the CIDR block 10.0.0.0/24. You are running out of IP addresses in this subnet due to autoscaling. You need to increase the size of the subnet to 10.0.0.0/20. How can you achieve this with minimal disruption?
options: Use the Google Cloud Console or `gcloud compute networks subnets expand-ip-range` command to increase the subnet size dynamically.
Delete the existing subnet and recreate it with the /20 CIDR block.
Create a new VPC network and peer it to the old one.
Enable Alias IP ranges on the existing VM instances.
correctAnswers: Use the Google Cloud Console or `gcloud compute networks subnets expand-ip-range` command to increase the subnet size dynamically.

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud VPC allows you to dynamically expand the IP address range of a subnet without any downtime or disruption to existing resources, as long as the new CIDR block encompasses the old one and does not conflict with other subnets.

why other options are wrong.Delete the existing subnet and recreate: Deleting the subnet would require deleting all VMs inside it, causing major downtime.
why other options are wrong.Create a new VPC network and peer it to: This is unnecessarily complex and does not solve the problem of running out of IPs in the specific target subnet.
why other options are wrong.Enable Alias IP ranges on the existing V: Alias IPs allocate secondary IPs to specific VMs; they do not expand the overall subnet capacity for new VM creation.

questions.questionText: You have deployed Compute Engine virtual machines in a private subnet. These instances do not have external public IP addresses assigned. However, they need to download software updates from a public repository on the internet. Which Google Cloud networking service should you configure to enable this secure outbound access?
options: Cloud NAT
Private Google Access
External Application Load Balancer
Cloud Router
correctAnswers: Cloud NAT

explanation.general explanation: Cloud NAT (Network Address Translation) allows VM instances without external IP addresses to connect out to the public internet for tasks like downloading updates, while simultaneously denying unsolicited inbound connections, preserving security.

why other options are wrong.Private Google Access: Private Google Access only provides access to internal Google APIs (like Cloud Storage), not to third-party public internet repositories.
why other options are wrong.External Application Load Balancer: Load balancers manage inbound traffic coming from the internet, not outbound internet access for private VMs.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Router: While Cloud NAT requires a Cloud Router to function, the Cloud Router itself only manages BGP routes; Cloud NAT performs the actual IP translation.

questions.questionText: A serverless application deployed on Cloud Run needs to securely query a highly sensitive Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database. To adhere to security policies, the Cloud SQL instance has been configured with a private internal IP address only. How can you connect the Cloud Run service to the database?
options: Configure a Serverless VPC Access connector in the same region.
Enable Private Google Access on the default VPC.
Set up Cloud NAT to route traffic from Cloud Run to the database.
Use a Global External Application Load Balancer to proxy the connection.
correctAnswers: Configure a Serverless VPC Access connector in the same region.

explanation.general explanation: Serverless VPC Access allows serverless environments, such as Cloud Run, App Engine standard, and Cloud Functions, to connect directly to a VPC network securely using internal IP addresses. This is required to reach private resources like an internal-only Cloud SQL database.

why other options are wrong.Enable Private Google Access on the defa: Private Google Access allows VPC VMs to reach Google APIs, but it does not bridge serverless environments into a VPC.
why other options are wrong.Set up Cloud NAT to route traffic from C: Cloud NAT is for outbound internet connectivity from a VPC, not for inbound serverless-to-VPC routing.
why other options are wrong.Use a Global External Application Load B: An external load balancer uses public IPs and would expose the traffic to the internet, violating the strict internal security policy.

questions.questionText: Your organization is performing a cost optimization review on its network architecture. You are currently serving large, non-critical static files to global users using an External Application Load Balancer. You want to significantly reduce outbound data egress costs and are willing to accept slightly higher latencies. Which two actions should you take?
options: Switch the load balancer configuration to use the Standard Network Service Tier.
Configure Cloud CDN on the load balancer backend.
Switch the load balancer configuration to use the Premium Network Service Tier.
Use an Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer instead.
Configure the Cloud Router to use static routing.
correctAnswers: Switch the load balancer configuration to use the Standard Network Service Tier.
Configure Cloud CDN on the load balancer backend.

explanation.general explanation: To reduce network costs, you can use the Standard Network Service Tier, which routes traffic over the cheaper public internet (transit ISPs) rather than Google's premium global backbone. Additionally, enabling Cloud CDN caches static content at the edge, drastically reducing the amount of data egressing from the backend servers.

why other options are wrong.Switch the load balancer configuration t: The Premium tier is the highest performance option but also the most expensive.
why other options are wrong.Use an Internal passthrough Network Load: Internal load balancers cannot serve traffic to global users on the public internet.
why other options are wrong.Configure the Cloud Router to use static: Cloud Router manages hybrid VPN/Interconnect routes; it has no impact on external load balancer egress costs.

questions.questionText: You are hosting a legacy application that relies on persistent TCP connections with secure SSL encryption. You want to terminate the SSL connections at the Google Cloud edge globally to offload the decryption workload from your backend instances. Which load balancer is specifically designed for this non-HTTP TCP traffic?
options: External proxy Network Load Balancer (SSL Proxy)
Global External Application Load Balancer
External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
correctAnswers: External proxy Network Load Balancer (SSL Proxy)

explanation.general explanation: The External proxy Network Load Balancer (SSL Proxy) terminates SSL/TLS connections at Google's global edge for non-HTTP TCP traffic. This offloads the intensive decryption work from your backend instances and provides a faster initial handshake for clients globally.

why other options are wrong.Global External Application Load Balance: This is specifically designed for HTTP and HTTPS traffic, whereas the scenario dictates non-HTTP TCP traffic.
why other options are wrong.External passthrough Network Load Balanc: A passthrough load balancer does not terminate connections; SSL decryption would have to be handled by the backend instances themselves.
why other options are wrong.Internal Application Load Balancer: This is strictly for internal traffic and cannot accept connections from external clients.

questions.questionText: Which Google Cloud load balancing solution provides native integration with Google Cloud Armor for Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) protection and Web Application Firewall (WAF) capabilities at the global edge?
options: Global External Application Load Balancer
External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
correctAnswers: Global External Application Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud Armor provides enterprise-grade WAF and DDoS mitigation. It is natively integrated with the Global External Application Load Balancer, allowing it to inspect incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic at the edge of Google's network before it reaches your backends.

why other options are wrong.External passthrough Network Load Balanc: This is a Layer 4 passthrough balancer. Cloud Armor WAF capabilities (Layer 7 inspection) cannot be applied here.
why other options are wrong.Internal passthrough Network Load Balanc: This handles internal traffic, whereas Cloud Armor protects against external internet threats.
why other options are wrong.Internal Application Load Balancer: Internal load balancers are not exposed to the public internet, so they do not natively use Cloud Armor edge protection.

questions.questionText: In Google Cloud, what is the scope of a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network, and what is the scope of its associated subnets?
options: A VPC is a global resource; subnets are regional resources.
A VPC is a regional resource; subnets are zonal resources.
Both the VPC and subnets are global resources.
Both the VPC and subnets are regional resources.
correctAnswers: A VPC is a global resource; subnets are regional resources.

explanation.general explanation: In Google Cloud architecture, a VPC network is a global resource, meaning it can span across multiple regions worldwide. However, individual subnets created within that VPC are strictly regional resources and cannot span across multiple regions.

why other options are wrong.A VPC is a regional resource; subnets ar: Unlike AWS, GCP VPCs are global, and subnets span all zones within a region, they are not restricted to a single zone.
why other options are wrong.Both the VPC and subnets are global reso: Subnets cannot cross regional boundaries; they are tied to a specific geographic region.
why other options are wrong.Both the VPC and subnets are regional re: The VPC itself is global and acts as a container for regional subnets.

questions.questionText: You need to create a VPC firewall rule that allows inbound HTTP traffic to a specific cluster of backend web servers. According to Google Cloud security best practices, what is the most secure and robust way to identify these specific target VMs in the firewall rule?
options: Use the target Service Account associated with the web servers.
Use a target Network Tag like 'web-server'.
Specify the target internal IP addresses of the web servers.
Apply the rule to all instances in the VPC.
correctAnswers: Use the target Service Account associated with the web servers.

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud strongly recommends using Service Accounts as targets in firewall rules instead of network tags. Service accounts enforce strict, identity-based access control tied to IAM permissions, whereas network tags can be arbitrarily added or modified by anyone with basic compute permissions.

why other options are wrong.Use a target Network Tag like 'web-serve: Network tags are prone to human error and offer weak security because any user with instance edit rights can change a tag.
why other options are wrong.Specify the target internal IP addresses: Hardcoding IP addresses is inflexible and breaks easily in auto-scaling cloud environments where IPs change frequently.
why other options are wrong.Apply the rule to all instances in the V: This violates the principle of least privilege by exposing every machine in the VPC to HTTP traffic.

questions.questionText: You have three distinct VPC networks: VPC A, VPC B, and VPC C. VPC A is peered with VPC B. VPC B is peered with VPC C. However, VMs in VPC A cannot ping VMs in VPC C. What are two fundamental constraints of VPC Network Peering that explain this behavior?
options: VPC Network Peering does not support transitive routing.
You must explicitly configure a peering connection directly between VPC A and VPC C.
VPC Peering requires Cloud Router to exchange BGP routes across a third network.
VPC Peering only supports TCP traffic; ICMP (ping) is blocked by default.
VPC Peering cannot connect networks in different regions.
correctAnswers: VPC Network Peering does not support transitive routing.
You must explicitly configure a peering connection directly between VPC A and VPC C.

explanation.general explanation: A fundamental rule of Google Cloud VPC Network Peering is that routing is not transitive. If VPC A peers with B, and B peers with C, VPC A does not automatically gain access to C. To establish connectivity between A and C, you must configure an explicit, direct peering connection between them.

why other options are wrong.VPC Peering requires Cloud Router to exc: VPC peering natively exchanges subnet routes automatically; it does not require Cloud Router or BGP.
why other options are wrong.VPC Peering only supports TCP traffic; I: VPC peering supports all protocols (including ICMP/ping), provided firewall rules allow it.
why other options are wrong.VPC Peering cannot connect networks in d: VPC peering bridges global networks and fully supports cross-region connectivity.

questions.questionText: Your company uses a high-performance, internal-only messaging system based on UDP. The backend instances are spread across multiple zones within the europe-west1 region. You need to distribute internal traffic evenly among these instances. Which load balancer is designed for this exact use case?
options: Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
External passthrough Network Load Balancer
External proxy Network Load Balancer
correctAnswers: Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: The Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer is a Layer 4 regional load balancer that distributes traffic among internal VM instances in the same region. It supports both TCP and UDP traffic, making it the perfect choice for internal UDP messaging systems.

why other options are wrong.Internal Application Load Balancer: This load balancer operates at Layer 7 and only supports HTTP/HTTPS, not UDP.
why other options are wrong.External passthrough Network Load Balanc: This balances traffic coming from the public internet, whereas the scenario specifies an internal-only messaging system.
why other options are wrong.External proxy Network Load Balancer: This proxy balancer is for external TCP traffic, does not support UDP, and is not internal.

questions.questionText: You are hosting an external TCP-based application. A strict security compliance rule requires that your backend VM instances log the original, unproxied client IP address directly at the network layer, without relying on HTTP headers like X-Forwarded-For. Which load balancer natively preserves the client source IP in this manner?
options: External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Global External Application Load Balancer
External proxy Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
correctAnswers: External passthrough Network Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: The External passthrough Network Load Balancer is not a proxy. It uses Maglev routing to simply forward packets to the backend instances. Because the packets are passed through unaltered, the backend VMs natively see the original client source IP address at the network packet level.

why other options are wrong.Global External Application Load Balance: This is a proxy load balancer. It terminates the connection and creates a new one to the backend, changing the network-level IP. (It passes the original IP in the X-Forwarded-For HTTP header, but the scenario restricts this).
why other options are wrong.External proxy Network Load Balancer: Like all proxies, it terminates the TCP connection and masks the client's network-level IP (unless PROXY protocol is used, which adds complexity).
why other options are wrong.Internal Application Load Balancer: This is an internal load balancer and does not handle external internet clients.

questions.questionText: When implementing a Shared VPC, resources are divided between different projects. Which statement correctly describes the architectural placement of networks and compute resources?
options: The Host project contains the shared VPC networks and subnets, while the Service projects contain the compute resources (like VMs).
The Service projects contain the shared VPC networks and subnets, while the Host project contains the compute resources.
Both Host and Service projects contain their own independent VPC networks that are peered together.
The Host project manages Cloud IAM, and the Service projects manage both networks and compute.
correctAnswers: The Host project contains the shared VPC networks and subnets, while the Service projects contain the compute resources (like VMs).

explanation.general explanation: In a Shared VPC architecture, the central 'Host project' owns the shared VPC network, its subnets, routes, and firewalls. Application teams use 'Service projects' to deploy their compute resources (like Compute Engine instances or GKE clusters), attaching them to the subnets located in the Host project.

why other options are wrong.The Service projects contain the shared: This is exactly reversed. Service projects consume networks; Host projects provide them.
why other options are wrong.Both Host and Service projects contain t: This describes VPC Network Peering, which is a completely different networking topology than Shared VPC.
While IAM is important, Shared VPC specifically centralizes networking resources, not just IAM policies.

questions.questionText: Your team needs to assign IP addresses directly from a VPC subnet to individual pods running inside Kubernetes on Compute Engine instances. This ensures the pods are natively routable within the VPC network without complex NAT rules. Which Compute Engine networking feature makes this possible?
options: Alias IP ranges
Cloud NAT
Static External IP addresses
Shared VPC subnets
correctAnswers: Alias IP ranges

explanation.general explanation: Alias IP ranges allow you to assign multiple internal IP addresses from a subnet's range to a single virtual machine's network interface. Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) uses Alias IPs heavily to natively assign routable VPC IP addresses to individual pods running on the worker node VMs.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT translates private IPs to public IPs for internet access; it does not assign sub-IPs to container pods.
why other options are wrong.Static External IP addresses: These assign public internet IP addresses to VMs, not internal routable IPs for containers.
why other options are wrong.Shared VPC subnets: While you can deploy GKE on a Shared VPC, the specific feature that allows pods to get their own IPs is Alias IP ranges.

questions.questionText: You are configuring a Global External Application Load Balancer to serve web traffic. Which two fundamental configuration components must be created to route incoming HTTP requests to your target backend VMs?
options: A Backend Service containing health checks and instance groups.
A URL Map to route requests to the appropriate backend service.
A Cloud Router configured with BGP.
A Cloud NAT gateway attached to the frontend IP.
A Serverless VPC Access connector.
correctAnswers: A Backend Service containing health checks and instance groups.
A URL Map to route requests to the appropriate backend service.

explanation.general explanation: To set up an Application Load Balancer, you must define a Backend Service (which groups the target instances and applies health checks to ensure they are available) and a URL Map (which acts as the central routing rules engine, determining which URL paths map to which Backend Services).

Cloud Router is used for dynamic hybrid networking (VPN/Interconnect), not for configuring Layer 7 load balancers.
why other options are wrong.A Cloud NAT gateway attached to the fron: Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access. Load balancers handle inbound traffic and are not attached to Cloud NAT.
This is used for connecting Serverless (Cloud Run) to a VPC, not for configuring external load balancers.

questions.questionText: A developer wants to create a single subnet with the IP range 10.5.0.0/16 and spread Compute Engine instances using that exact subnet across the `us-central1` and `europe-west1` regions for disaster recovery. As a Cloud Architect, what should you advise?
options: This is not possible because subnets are strictly regional resources and cannot span multiple regions.
This is possible if the VPC is configured with Global Dynamic Routing.
This is possible if they use an Auto mode VPC network.
This is not possible because the 10.x.x.x range is reserved for Google APIs.
correctAnswers: This is not possible because subnets are strictly regional resources and cannot span multiple regions.

explanation.general explanation: In Google Cloud, a VPC network is global, but subnets are strictly regional. A single subnet (and its associated IP range) cannot span across two different geographic regions like `us-central1` and `europe-west1`. You must create separate subnets in each region.

why other options are wrong.This is possible if the VPC is configure: Global dynamic routing affects how Cloud Router advertises routes over a VPN/Interconnect; it does not change the physical limitations of a subnet.
why other options are wrong.This is possible if they use an Auto mod: Auto mode creates distinct subnets in every region with different IP ranges; it does not stretch one subnet across regions.
10.0.0.0/8 is standard RFC 1918 private IP space perfectly valid for VPC subnets. It is not reserved exclusively for Google APIs.

questions.questionText: Your enterprise owns a block of public IP addresses and wishes to migrate them to Google Cloud so they can be assigned to your External Application Load Balancers. Does Google Cloud networking support this, and if so, what is the feature called?
options: Yes, using the Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) feature.
Yes, using Private Google Access.
No, Google Cloud only allows you to use IPs generated by Google.
No, public IPs must be purchased directly through Cloud DNS.
correctAnswers: Yes, using the Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) feature.

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud supports Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP). This feature allows you to provision and use your own public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses for Google Cloud resources, such as external load balancers and Compute Engine instances, enabling you to maintain IP reputation and hardcoded firewall whitelists.

Private Google Access is for internal IPs reaching Google services, completely unrelated to public IP ownership.
why other options are wrong.No, Google Cloud only allows you to use: Google does allow bringing external public IP blocks via BYOIP.
why other options are wrong.No, public IPs must be purchased directl: Cloud DNS manages domain names, not IP block procurement or BYOIP.

questions.questionText: Referencing the Mountkirk Games case study: They are moving their game backend to a microservices architecture. They require global HTTP load balancing to direct users to the nearest regional backend instances using a single Anycast IP. Which load balancing solution aligns perfectly with Mountkirk Games' requirements?
options: Global External Application Load Balancer
External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
Global external proxy Network Load Balancer
correctAnswers: Global External Application Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: The Mountkirk Games case study requires global scaling for web/HTTP traffic to seamlessly direct players to the closest healthy backend. The Global External Application Load Balancer natively provides a global Anycast IP address and routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic to the nearest region with available capacity.

why other options are wrong.External passthrough Network Load Balanc: This is a regional load balancer. It cannot provide a global Anycast IP or route HTTP traffic globally.
why other options are wrong.Internal Application Load Balancer: This load balancer is for internal VPC traffic and cannot be accessed by external game clients on the internet.
why other options are wrong.Global external proxy Network Load Balan: This is for non-HTTP TCP/SSL proxying. Since they need HTTP load balancing specifically, the Application LB is correct.

questions.questionText: When you create a new Google Cloud project, a 'default' VPC network is automatically provisioned. What is the recommended best practice regarding the default VPC network for production enterprise deployments?
options: Delete the default VPC and create a Custom mode VPC network.
Leave it as is and use it to deploy production resources to save time.
Upgrade the default VPC to Premium tier.
Convert the default VPC to a Shared VPC Host project immediately.
correctAnswers: Delete the default VPC and create a Custom mode VPC network.

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud architectural best practices dictate that the default VPC (which is an Auto mode VPC with predefined firewall rules) should be deleted. For production workloads, you should always create a Custom mode VPC to ensure strict control over IP address ranges and security policies.

why other options are wrong.Leave it as is and use it to deploy prod: Using the default VPC in production is highly discouraged due to overlapping IP risks and overly permissive default firewall rules.
VPCs themselves do not have a 'Premium tier' (Network Service Tiers apply to routing external traffic).
why other options are wrong.Convert the default VPC to a Shared VPC: Even in Shared VPC setups, you should use a Custom mode VPC, not the default Auto mode VPC.

questions.questionText: Your e-commerce application has a single frontend domain. However, you want traffic for `/images` to be routed to a specific backend bucket containing static assets, and traffic for `/api` to be routed to a managed instance group of application servers. Which load balancing feature enables this?
options: URL Maps (Path-based routing)
Cloud DNS routing policies
Network Endpoint Groups (NEGs)
VPC Route tables
correctAnswers: URL Maps (Path-based routing)

explanation.general explanation: URL Maps are a core configuration component of Layer 7 Application Load Balancers. They allow you to define path-based routing rules, sending HTTP requests like `/images` to a Cloud Storage backend and `/api` to a compute backend based entirely on the URL path.

why other options are wrong.Cloud DNS routing policies: DNS operates before the HTTP request is even made and routes based on domain name, not URL paths.
why other options are wrong.Network Endpoint Groups (NEGs): NEGs define endpoints (like containers or serverless apps) to load balance to, but they don't perform the URL routing logic.
why other options are wrong.VPC Route tables: VPC Route tables handle Layer 3 IP packet routing, not Layer 7 HTTP URL path routing.

questions.questionText: You are configuring a load balancer and need to ensure that traffic is not routed to VM instances that have crashed or stopped responding. How does the Google Cloud load balancer determine if an instance is capable of receiving traffic?
options: It uses Health Checks to periodically probe the backend instances.
It monitors the CPU utilization using Cloud Monitoring.
It checks the status of the VM in the Compute Engine console.
It relies on the instances to push a 'ready' signal to the load balancer.
correctAnswers: It uses Health Checks to periodically probe the backend instances.

explanation.general explanation: Health Checks are configured on backend services to actively probe the backend instances (e.g., via HTTP pings or TCP connection attempts) at regular intervals. If an instance fails the health check, the load balancer marks it as unhealthy and stops routing new traffic to it until it recovers.

why other options are wrong.It monitors the CPU utilization using Cl: CPU utilization is used for auto-scaling instance groups, but it does not tell the load balancer if the application software has crashed or frozen.
why other options are wrong.It checks the status of the VM in the Co: A VM can be 'Running' in the console but the web server software inside might be broken. Health checks verify the software layer.
why other options are wrong.It relies on the instances to push a 're: Load balancer health checking is an active, 'pull' mechanism (probing), not a push from the instance.

questions.questionText: Your team needs to establish outbound internet access for several private VMs across multiple regions. They plan to deploy Cloud NAT. Which statement correctly describes the architectural scope of a Cloud NAT gateway?
options: A single Cloud NAT gateway operates within a single region and is attached to a regional Cloud Router.
A single Cloud NAT gateway operates globally across the entire VPC.
A Cloud NAT gateway must be attached to a specific individual VM instance.
A Cloud NAT gateway is a physical appliance installed in a Google colocation facility.
correctAnswers: A single Cloud NAT gateway operates within a single region and is attached to a regional Cloud Router.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud NAT is a regional service. To provide NAT for VMs in a region, you must create a Cloud NAT gateway and attach it to a Cloud Router located in that specific region. If you have VMs in multiple regions, you must deploy a separate Cloud NAT gateway in each region.

why other options are wrong.A single Cloud NAT gateway operates glob: Cloud NAT cannot span regions. It only provides translation for subnets in its specific region.
why other options are wrong.A Cloud NAT gateway must be attached to: Cloud NAT operates at the VPC/subnet level via Cloud Router, not attached to an individual VM.
why other options are wrong.A Cloud NAT gateway is a physical applia: Cloud NAT is a software-defined, fully managed service (Andromeda), not a physical appliance.

questions.questionText: To optimize costs and performance, Google Cloud allows you to choose between the Premium and Standard Network Service Tiers. Which two statements accurately differentiate these tiers?
options: Premium Tier routes traffic over Google's high-performance global network backbone.
Standard Tier routes outbound traffic to the internet over transit ISP networks.
Premium Tier is restricted to routing traffic only within a single geographic region.
Standard Tier supports Global External Application Load Balancers with global Anycast IPs.
Standard Tier is the default option selected when creating new projects.
correctAnswers: Premium Tier routes traffic over Google's high-performance global network backbone.
Standard Tier routes outbound traffic to the internet over transit ISP networks.

explanation.general explanation: The Premium Network Service Tier routes user traffic over Google's highly reliable, low-latency global fiber network. The Standard Tier delivers traffic over standard internet service providers (ISPs), which is cheaper but less predictable and limited to regional deployments.

why other options are wrong.Premium Tier is restricted to routing tr: This describes the Standard Tier limitation. Premium Tier is inherently global.
why other options are wrong.Standard Tier supports Global External A: Standard Tier cannot support Global Load Balancers because it is strictly regional.
why other options are wrong.Standard Tier is the default option sele: Premium Tier is actually the default setting in Google Cloud to ensure the highest performance.
